**Barbados**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-7) is an [island nation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island_country "Island country") in the [Caribbean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean "Caribbean") located in the [Atlantic Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Ocean "Atlantic Ocean"). It is part of the [Lesser Antilles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lesser_Antilles "Lesser Antilles") of the [West Indies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Indies "West Indies") and is the southern and easternmost island of the [Caribbean region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_region "Caribbean region"). It lies on the boundary of the [South American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_American_Plate "South American Plate") and [Caribbean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Plate "Caribbean Plate") plates. Its capital and largest city is [Bridgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridgetown "Bridgetown").

Inhabited by [Kalinago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island_Caribs "Island Caribs") people since the 13th century, and prior to that by other [Indigenous peoples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_of_the_Americas "Indigenous peoples of the Americas"), the island was originally named Ichirouganaim.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-ABC_News-8) It was claimed for the [Crown of Castile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crown_of_Castile "Crown of Castile") by Spanish navigators in the late 15th century, who named it "Barbudos", and it first appeared on a Spanish map in 1511.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Spanish_Main-9) The [Portuguese Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_Empire "Portuguese Empire") claimed the island between 1532 and 1536, but abandoned it in 1620 with their only remnants being the introduction of wild boars intended as a supply of meat whenever the island was visited. The indigenous population was mostly sold into slavery, killed or died of disease by this time.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-ABC_News-8)

An [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_England "Kingdom of England") ship, the _Olive Blossom_, arrived in Barbados on 14 May 1625; its men took possession of the island in the name of [King James I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_VI_and_I "James VI and I"). In 1627, the first permanent settlers arrived from England, and Barbados became an [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_overseas_possessions "English overseas possessions") and later [British colony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_colonisation_of_the_Americas#British_Caribbean_colonies "British colonisation of the Americas").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-10) During this period, the colony operated on a [plantation economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plantation_economy "Plantation economy"), relying initially on the labour of [Irish indentured servants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_indentured_servants "Irish indentured servants")[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-11) and subsequently [African slaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_slave_trade "Atlantic slave trade") who worked on the island's plantations. Slavery continued until it was phased out through most of the [British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire "British Empire") by the [Slavery Abolition Act 1833](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavery_Abolition_Act_1833 "Slavery Abolition Act 1833"). The descendants of these enslaved Africans now account for over 90% of the island's population.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-12)

On 30 November 1966, Barbados moved toward political independence and assumed the status of a [Commonwealth realm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_realm "Commonwealth realm"), becoming a sovereign state with [Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_II "Elizabeth II") as [Queen of Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monarchy_of_Barbados "Monarchy of Barbados"). On 30 November 2021, Barbados transitioned to a [republic within the Commonwealth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republics_in_the_Commonwealth_of_Nations "Republics in the Commonwealth of Nations"), replacing its monarchy with a ceremonial president.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-13)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-14)

Barbados is ranked as one of the Caribbean's leading [tourist destinations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism "Tourism").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-15)

## Etymology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Barbados&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Etymology")]

The name "Barbados" is from either the [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language") term _os barbados_ or the Spanish equivalent, _los barbados_, both meaning "the bearded ones".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-16)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-17) It is unclear whether "bearded" refers to the long, hanging roots of the bearded [fig tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fig_tree "Fig tree") (_[Ficus citrifolia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ficus\_citrifolia "Ficus citrifolia")_), a species of [banyan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banyan "Banyan") indigenous to the island, or to the allegedly bearded [Kalinago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalinago "Kalinago") (Island Caribs) who once inhabited the island, or, more fancifully, to a visual impression of a beard formed by the sea foam that sprays over the outlying coral reefs. In 1519, a map produced by the [Genoese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genoa "Genoa") mapmaker [Visconte Maggiolo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visconte_Maggiolo "Visconte Maggiolo") showed and named Barbados in its correct position.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-18) Furthermore, the island of [Barbuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbuda "Barbuda") in the [Leewards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leeward_Islands "Leeward Islands") is very similar in name and was once named "Las Barbudas" by the Spanish.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The original name for Barbados in the [Pre-Columbian era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pre-Columbian_era "Pre-Columbian era") was _Ichirouganaim_, according to accounts by descendants of the Indigenous [Arawakan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arawakan_languages "Arawakan languages")-speaking tribes in other regional areas, with possible translations including "Red land with white teeth"[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-19) or "Redstone island with teeth outside (reefs)"[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-20) or simply "Teeth".[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-21)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-22)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-23)

Colloquially, Barbadians refer to their home island as "Bim" or other nicknames associated with Barbados, including "Bimshire". The origin is uncertain, but several theories exist. The [National Cultural Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Cultural_Foundation "National Cultural Foundation") of Barbados says that "Bim" was a word commonly used by [slaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slave "Slave"), and that it derives from the [Igbo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igbo_language "Igbo language") term _bém_ from _bé mụ́_ meaning "my home, kindred, kind";[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Carrington,_Sean_2007_25-24) the Igbo phoneme [[e]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Igbo "Help:IPA/Igbo") in the Igbo orthography is very close to [/ɪ/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-25) The name could have arisen due to the relatively large percentage of [Igbo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igbo_people "Igbo people") slaves from modern-day southeastern [Nigeria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria "Nigeria") arriving in Barbados in the 18th century.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-26)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-27) The words "Bim" and "Bimshire" are recorded in the _[Oxford English Dictionary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford\_English\_Dictionary "Oxford English Dictionary")_ and _[Chambers Twentieth Century Dictionaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chambers\_Dictionary "Chambers Dictionary")_. Another possible source for "Bim" is reported to be in the _Agricultural Reporter_ of 25 April 1868, where the Rev. N. Greenidge (father of one of the island's most famous scholars, [Abel Hendy Jones Greenidge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abel_Hendy_Jones_Greenidge "Abel Hendy Jones Greenidge")) suggested that Bimshire was "introduced by an old planter listing it as a county of England". Expressly named were "Wiltshire, Hampshire, Berkshire and Bimshire".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Carrington,_Sean_2007_25-24) Lastly, in the _Daily Argosy_ (of Demerara, i.e. Guyana) of 1652, there is a reference to Bim as a possible corruption of "Byam", the name of a Royalist leader against the Parliamentarians. That source suggested the followers of Byam became known as "Bims" and that this became a word for all Barbadians.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Carrington,_Sean_2007_25-24)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Barbados&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

Main article: [History of Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Barbados "History of Barbados")

### Geological history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Barbados&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Geological history")]

Around 700,000 years ago, the island emerged from the ocean as a body of soft rock known as a [diapir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diapir "Diapir") rose from the mantle beneath its present-day location. This process is still ongoing, raising Barbados at an average rate of 30 centimetres per thousand years.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-earthmagazine-28) Dozens of inland sea reefs still dominate coastal features within terraces and cliffs on the island.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-earthmagazine-28)

### Pre-colonial period

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Barbados&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Pre-colonial period")]

Archeological evidence suggests humans may have first settled or visited the island c.1600 BC.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Encylopedia_Britannica-_Barbados-29)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-30)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-31) More permanent [Amerindian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amerindian "Amerindian") settlement of Barbados dates to about the 4th to 7th centuries AD, by a group known as the [Saladoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saladoid "Saladoid")-Barrancoid.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-32) Settlements of [Arawaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arawaks "Arawaks") from South America appeared by around 800 AD and again in the 12th–13th century.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Encylopedia_Britannica-_Barbados-29) The [Kalinago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalinago "Kalinago") (called "[Caribs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island_Caribs "Island Caribs")" by the Spanish) visited the island regularly, although there is no evidence of permanent settlement.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-33)

### European arrival

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Barbados&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: European arrival")]

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a7/1632_Cardona_Descripcion_Indias_%2811%29.jpg/250px-1632_Cardona_Descripcion_Indias_%2811%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:1632_Cardona_Descripcion_Indias_(11).jpg)

Spanish map of the island (1632)

It is uncertain which European nation arrived first in Barbados, which probably would have been at some point in the 15th century or 16th century. One lesser-known source points to earlier revealed works antedating contemporary sources, indicating it could have been the Spanish.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Spanish_Main-9) Many, if not most, believe the [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Portugal_(1415%E2%80%931578) "History of Portugal (1415–1578)"), en route to Brazil,[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-34)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-35) were the first Europeans to come upon the island. The island was largely ignored by Europeans, though Spanish slave raiding is thought to have reduced the native population, with many fleeing to other islands.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Encylopedia_Britannica-_Barbados-29)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-36)

### English settlement in the 17th century

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Barbados&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: English settlement in the 17th century")]

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0e/GEORGE_WASHINGTON_HOUSE_-_BARBADOS.jpg/250px-GEORGE_WASHINGTON_HOUSE_-_BARBADOS.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:GEORGE_WASHINGTON_HOUSE_-_BARBADOS.jpg)

[George Washington House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Washington_House_(Barbados) "George Washington House (Barbados)") was visited by [George Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Washington "George Washington") in 1751, in what is believed to have been his only trip outside the present-day United States.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-37)

The first English ship, which had arrived on 14 May 1625, was captained by John Powell. The first settlement began on 17 February 1627, near what is now [Holetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holetown "Holetown") (formerly Jamestown, after King James I of England),[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-38) by a group led by John Powell's younger brother, [Henry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Powell_(governor) "Henry Powell (governor)"), consisting of 80 settlers and 10 English [indentured labourers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indentured_servitude "Indentured servitude").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-39) Some sources state that some Africans were among these first settlers.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Encylopedia_Britannica-_Barbados-29)

The settlement was established as a [proprietary colony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proprietary_colony "Proprietary colony") and funded by Sir [William Courten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Courten "William Courten"), a [City of London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_London "City of London") merchant who acquired the title to Barbados and several other islands. The first colonists were actually tenants, and much of the profits of their labour returned to Courten and his company.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-40) Courten's title was later transferred to [James Hay, 1st Earl of Carlisle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Hay,_1st_Earl_of_Carlisle "James Hay, 1st Earl of Carlisle"), in what was called the "Great Barbados Robbery".[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-41) Carlisle then chose as governor [Henry Powell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Powell_(governor) "Henry Powell (governor)"), who established the [House of Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados_House_of_Assembly "Barbados House of Assembly") in 1639, in an effort to appease the planters, who might otherwise have opposed his controversial appointment.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Encylopedia_Britannica-_Barbados-29)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Slavery_and_Economy_in_Barbados-42)

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/English_Quakers_Tobacco_Planters_and_Slaves%2C_Barbados%2C_17th_cent._%28colorized%29.jpg/250px-English_Quakers_Tobacco_Planters_and_Slaves%2C_Barbados%2C_17th_cent._%28colorized%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:English_Quakers_Tobacco_Planters_and_Slaves,_Barbados,_17th_cent._(colorized).jpg)

English tobacco planters and slaves in Barbados, 17th century

In the period 1640–1660, the West Indies attracted more than two-thirds of the total number of English emigrants to the Americas. By 1650, there were 44,000 settlers in the West Indies, as compared to 12,000 on the [Chesapeake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chesapeake_Bay "Chesapeake Bay") and 23,000 in [New England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England "New England"). Most English arrivals were indentured. After five years of labour, they were given "freedom dues" of about £10, usually in goods. Before the mid-1630s, they also received 5 to 10 acres (2 to 4 hectares) of land, but after that time the island filled and there was no more free land. During the [Cromwellian era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interregnum_(England) "Interregnum (England)") (1650s) this included a large number of prisoners-of-war, vagrants and people who were illicitly kidnapped, who were forcibly transported to the island and sold as servants. These last two groups were predominantly Irish, as several thousand were infamously rounded up by English merchants and sold into servitude in Barbados and other Caribbean islands during this period, a practice that came to be known as being _Barbadosed_.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Slavery_and_Economy_in_Barbados-42)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-43) Cultivation of [sugar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugar "Sugar") was thus handled primarily by European indentured labour until it became difficult to bring more indentured servants from England.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-44)

[Parish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parishes_of_Barbados "Parishes of Barbados") registers from the 1650s show that, for the white population, there were four times as many deaths as marriages. The mainstay of the infant colony's economy was the growth export of tobacco, but tobacco prices eventually fell in the 1630s as Chesapeake production expanded.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Slavery_and_Economy_in_Barbados-42)

#### Effects of the English Civil War

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Barbados&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Effects of the English Civil War")]

Main articles: [English overseas possessions in the Wars of the Three Kingdoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_overseas_possessions_in_the_Wars_of_the_Three_Kingdoms "English overseas possessions in the Wars of the Three Kingdoms") and [Restoration in the English colonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Restoration_in_the_English_colonies "Restoration in the English colonies")

Around the same time, fighting during the [War of the Three Kingdoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_of_the_Three_Kingdoms "War of the Three Kingdoms") and the [Interregnum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interregnum_(England) "Interregnum (England)") spilled over into Barbados and Barbadian territorial waters. The island was not [involved in the war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_overseas_possessions_in_the_Wars_of_the_Three_Kingdoms "English overseas possessions in the Wars of the Three Kingdoms") until after the execution of [Charles I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_I_of_England "Charles I of England"), when the island's government fell under the control of Royalists (ironically the Governor, Philip Bell, remaining loyal to [Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_of_England "Parliament of England") while the Barbadian [House of Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Assembly "House of Assembly"), under the influence of Humphrey Walrond, supported [Charles II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_II_of_England "Charles II of England")). To try to bring the recalcitrant colony to heel, the [Commonwealth Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rump_Parliament#Commonwealth_of_England "Rump Parliament") passed an act on 3 October 1650 prohibiting trade between England and Barbados, and because the island also traded with the Netherlands, further [Navigation Acts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navigation_Acts "Navigation Acts") were passed, prohibiting any but English vessels trading with [Dutch colonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Empire#Atlantic "Dutch Empire"). These acts were a precursor to the [First Anglo-Dutch War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Anglo-Dutch_War "First Anglo-Dutch War"). The [Commonwealth of England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_England "Commonwealth of England") sent an invasion force under the command of [Sir George Ayscue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Ayscue "George Ayscue"), which arrived in October 1651. Ayscue, with a smaller force that included Scottish prisoners, surprised a larger force of Royalists, but had to resort to spying and diplomacy ultimately. On 11 January 1652, the Royalists in the House of Assembly led by [Lord Willoughby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Willoughby,_5th_Baron_Willoughby_of_Parham "Francis Willoughby, 5th Baron Willoughby of Parham") surrendered, which marked the end of royalist privateering as a major threat.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-45) The conditions of the surrender were incorporated into the [Charter of Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charter_of_Barbados?action=edit&redlink=1 "Charter of Barbados (page does not exist)") ([Treaty of Oistins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oistins#History "Oistins")), which was signed at the Mermaid's Inn, [Oistins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oistins "Oistins"), on 17 January 1652.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-46)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-47)

### Irish people in Barbados

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Barbados&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Irish people in Barbados")]

Main article: [Irish people in Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_people_in_Barbados "Irish people in Barbados")

Starting with [Cromwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Cromwell "Oliver Cromwell"), a large percentage of the white labourer population were indentured servants and involuntarily transported people from Ireland. Irish servants in Barbados were often treated poorly, and Barbadian planters gained a reputation for cruelty.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Monahan-48):55 The decreased appeal of an indenture on Barbados, combined with enormous demand for labour caused by sugar cultivation, led to the use of involuntary transportation to Barbados as a punishment for crimes, or for political prisoners, and also to the kidnapping of labourers who were deported to Barbados.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Monahan-48):55 Irish indentured servants were a significant portion of the population throughout the period when white servants were used for plantation labour in Barbados, and while a "steady stream" of Irish servants entered Barbados throughout the 17th century, Cromwellian efforts to [pacify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacification_(military_action) "Pacification (military action)") Ireland created a "veritable tidal wave" of Irish labourers who were sent to Barbados during the 1650s.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Monahan-48):56 Due to inadequate historical records, the total number of Irish labourers sent to Barbados is unknown, and estimates have been "highly contentious".[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Monahan-48):56 While one historical source estimated that as many as 50,000 Irish people were deported to either Barbados or Virginia during the 1650s. Another estimate that 12,000 Irish prisoners had arrived in Barbados by 1655 has been described by historian Richard B. Sheridan.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-49):236 According to historian [Thomas Bartlett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Bartlett_(historian) "Thomas Bartlett (historian)"), it is "generally accepted" that approximately 10,000 Irish were deported to the West Indies and approximately 40,000 came as voluntary indentured servants, while many also travelled as voluntary, un-indentured emigrants.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-50):256

#### The sugar revolution

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Barbados&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: The sugar revolution")]

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fd/Mercado_de_los_domingos%2C_donde_lo_esclavos_eran_intercambiados_por_otros_bienes_y_necesidades_%28Barbados_Museum%2C_Bridgetown%29.jpg/250px-Mercado_de_los_domingos%2C_donde_lo_esclavos_eran_intercambiados_por_otros_bienes_y_necesidades_%28Barbados_Museum%2C_Bridgetown%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mercado_de_los_domingos,_donde_lo_esclavos_eran_intercambiados_por_otros_bienes_y_necesidades_(Barbados_Museum,_Bridgetown).jpg)

Sunday market in Barbados during the colonial era

See also: [Indian slave trade between Barbados and South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_slave_trade_between_Barbados_and_South_Carolina "Indian slave trade between Barbados and South Carolina")

The introduction of [sugar cane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugar_cane "Sugar cane") from [Dutch Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Brazil "Dutch Brazil") in 1640[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-51) completely transformed society, the economy and the physical landscape.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-52) Barbados eventually had one of the world's biggest sugar industries.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-beyond-53) One group instrumental in ensuring the early success of the industry was the [Sephardic Jews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sephardi_Jews "Sephardi Jews"), who had originally been expelled from the [Iberian peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iberian_peninsula "Iberian peninsula"), to end up in [Dutch Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Brazil "Dutch Brazil").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-beyond-53) As the effects of the new crop increased, so did the shift in the ethnic composition of Barbados and surrounding islands.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Slavery_and_Economy_in_Barbados-42) The workable sugar plantation required a large investment and a great deal of heavy labour. At first, Dutch traders supplied the equipment, financing, and African slaves, in addition to transporting most of the sugar to Europe.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Slavery_and_Economy_in_Barbados-42)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Encylopedia_Britannica-_Barbados-29) In 1644, the population of Barbados was estimated at 30,000, of which about 800 were of African ancestry, with the remainder mainly of English ancestry. These English smallholders were eventually bought out and the island filled up with large sugar plantations worked by African slaves.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Encylopedia_Britannica-_Barbados-29) By 1660 there was near parity with 27,000 Black people and 26,000 White people. By 1666, at least 12,000 white smallholders had been bought out, died, or left the island, many choosing to emigrate to [Jamaica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaica "Jamaica") or the [American Colonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirteen_Colonies "Thirteen Colonies") (notably the Carolinas).[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Encylopedia_Britannica-_Barbados-29) As a result, Barbados enacted a [slave code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados_Slave_Code "Barbados Slave Code") as a way of legislatively controlling its enslaved Black population.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-54) The law's text was influential in laws in other colonies.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-55)

By 1680 there were 20,000 free whites and 46,000 enslaved Africans;[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Encylopedia_Britannica-_Barbados-29) by 1724, there were 18,000 free whites and 55,000 enslaved Africans.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Slavery_and_Economy_in_Barbados-42)

### 18th and 19th centuries

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Barbados&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 18th and 19th centuries")]

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a6/Bussa_statue.png/250px-Bussa_statue.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bussa_statue.png)

[Statue of Bussa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emancipation_Statue_(Haggett_Hall,_Barbados) "Emancipation Statue (Haggett Hall, Barbados)"), Bridgetown. Bussa led the largest slave rebellion in Barbadian history.

The harsh conditions endured by the slaves resulted in several planned slave rebellions, the largest of which was [Bussa's rebellion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bussa's_rebellion "Bussa's rebellion") in 1816 which was rapidly suppressed by the colonial authorities.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Encylopedia_Britannica-_Barbados-29) In 1819, another slave revolt broke out on Easter Day. The revolt was put down in blood, with heads being displayed on stakes. Nevertheless, the brutality of the repression shocked even England and strengthened the abolitionist movement.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-56) Growing opposition to slavery led to its abolition in the British Empire in 1833.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Encylopedia_Britannica-_Barbados-29) The [plantocracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plantocracy "Plantocracy") class retained control of political and economic power on the island, with most workers living in relative poverty.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Encylopedia_Britannica-_Barbados-29)

The [1780 hurricane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Hurricane_of_1780 "Great Hurricane of 1780") killed more than 4,000 people on Barbados.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-57)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-58) In 1854, a [cholera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cholera "Cholera") epidemic killed more than 20,000 inhabitants.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-59)

### 20th century before independence

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Barbados&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: 20th century before independence")]

Deep dissatisfaction with the situation on Barbados led many to emigrate.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Encylopedia_Britannica-_Barbados-29)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-60) Things came to a head in the 1930s during the [Great Depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression "Great Depression"), as Barbadians [began demanding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_West_Indian_labour_unrest_of_1934%E2%80%931939 "British West Indian labour unrest of 1934–1939") better conditions for workers, the legalisation of trade unions and a widening of the franchise, which at that point was limited to male property owners.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Encylopedia_Britannica-_Barbados-29) As a result of the increasing unrest the British sent a commission, called the [West Indies Royal Commission, or Moyne Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Report_of_West_India_Royal_Commission_(Moyne_Report) "Report of West India Royal Commission (Moyne Report)"), in 1938, which recommended enacting many of the requested reforms on the islands.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Encylopedia_Britannica-_Barbados-29) As a result, Afro-Barbadians began to play a much more prominent role in the colony's politics, with universal suffrage being introduced in 1950.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Encylopedia_Britannica-_Barbados-29)

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3c/Collectie_Nationaal_Museum_van_Wereldculturen_TM-60062011_De_hoofdstraat_van_Bridgetown_Barbados_fotograaf_niet_bekend.jpg/250px-Collectie_Nationaal_Museum_van_Wereldculturen_TM-60062011_De_hoofdstraat_van_Bridgetown_Barbados_fotograaf_niet_bekend.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Collectie_Nationaal_Museum_van_Wereldculturen_TM-60062011_De_hoofdstraat_van_Bridgetown_Barbados_fotograaf_niet_bekend.jpg)

Broad Street, Bridgetown in 1914

Prominent among these early activists was [Grantley Herbert Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grantley_Herbert_Adams "Grantley Herbert Adams"), who helped found the [Barbados Labour Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados_Labour_Party "Barbados Labour Party") (BLP) in 1938.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-61) He became the first Premier of Barbados in 1953, followed by fellow BLP-founder [Hugh Gordon Cummins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Gordon_Cummins "Hugh Gordon Cummins") from 1958 to 1961. A group of left-leaning politicians who advocated swifter moves to independence broke off from the BLP and founded the [Democratic Labour Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Labour_Party_(Barbados) "Democratic Labour Party (Barbados)") (DLP) in 1955.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-62)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-63) The DLP subsequently won the [1961 Barbadian general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1961_Barbadian_general_election "1961 Barbadian general election") and their leader [Errol Barrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Errol_Barrow "Errol Barrow") became premier.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Full internal self-government was enacted in 1961.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Encylopedia_Britannica-_Barbados-29) Barbados joined the short-lived British [West Indies Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Indies_Federation "West Indies Federation") from 1958 to 1962, later gaining full independence on 30 November 1966.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Encylopedia_Britannica-_Barbados-29) Errol Barrow became the country's first prime minister.

Barbados opted to remain within the [Commonwealth of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Nations "Commonwealth of Nations"). [Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_II "Elizabeth II") became [Queen of Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_of_Barbados "Queen of Barbados") and was represented locally by a [governor-general](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor-General_of_Barbados "Governor-General of Barbados").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-64).

### Post-independence era

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Barbados&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Post-independence era")]

The Barrow government sought to diversify the economy away from agriculture, seeking to boost industry and the tourism sector. Barbados was also at the forefront of regional integration efforts, spearheading the creation of [CARIFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CARIFTA "CARIFTA") and [CARICOM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CARICOM "CARICOM").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Encylopedia_Britannica-_Barbados-29) The DLP lost the [1976 Barbadian general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976_Barbadian_general_election "1976 Barbadian general election") to the BLP under [Tom Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Adams_(politician) "Tom Adams (politician)"). Adams adopted a more conservative and strongly pro-Western stance, allowing the Americans to use Barbados as the launchpad for their [invasion of Grenada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_invasion_of_Grenada "United States invasion of Grenada") in 1983.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-65) Adams died in office in 1985 and was replaced by [Harold Bernard St. John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harold_Bernard_St._John "Harold Bernard St. John"); however, St. John lost the [1986 Barbadian general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Barbadian_general_election "1986 Barbadian general election"), which saw the return of the DLP under Errol Barrow, who had been highly critical of the US intervention in Grenada. Barrow, too, died in office, and was replaced by [Lloyd Erskine Sandiford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd_Erskine_Sandiford "Lloyd Erskine Sandiford"), who remained Prime Minister until 1994.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

[Owen Arthur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Owen_Arthur "Owen Arthur") of the BLP won the [1994 Barbadian general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Barbadian_general_election "1994 Barbadian general election"), remaining prime minister until 2008.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-66) Arthur was a strong advocate of republicanism, though a planned referendum to replace Queen Elizabeth as Head of State in 2008 never took place.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-67) The DLP won the [2008 Barbadian general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Barbadian_general_election "2008 Barbadian general election"), but the new Prime Minister [David Thompson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Thompson_(Barbadian_politician) "David Thompson (Barbadian politician)") died in 2010 and was replaced by [Freundel Stuart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freundel_Stuart "Freundel Stuart"). The BLP returned to power [in 2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Barbadian_general_election "2018 Barbadian general election") under [Mia Mottley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mia_Mottley "Mia Mottley"), who became Barbados's first female prime minister.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-68)

#### Transition to republic

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Barbados&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Transition to republic")]

Main article: [Republicanism in Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republicanism_in_Barbados "Republicanism in Barbados")

The Government of Barbados announced on 15 September 2020 that it intended to become a republic by 30 November 2021, the 55th anniversary of its independence, resulting in the replacement of the [Barbadian monarchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbadian_monarchy "Barbadian monarchy") with a president elected through an [electoral college](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electoral_college "Electoral college").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-69)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-70) Barbados would then cease to be a [Commonwealth realm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_realm "Commonwealth realm"), but could maintain membership in the [Commonwealth of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Nations "Commonwealth of Nations"), like [Guyana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guyana "Guyana") and [Trinidad and Tobago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinidad_and_Tobago "Trinidad and Tobago").[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-71)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-72)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-73)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-74)

On 20 September 2021, just over a full year after the announcement for the transition was made, the [Constitution (Amendment) (No. 2) Bill, 2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_(Amendment)_(No._2)_Bill,_2021 "Constitution (Amendment) (No. 2) Bill, 2021") was introduced in the Parliament of Barbados. Passed on 6 October, the Bill made amendments to the Constitution of Barbados, introducing the office of the [president of Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Barbados "President of Barbados") to replace the role of [Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_II "Elizabeth II") as Queen of Barbados.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-75) The following week, on 12 October 2021, incumbent [Governor-General of Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor-General_of_Barbados "Governor-General of Barbados")[Sandra Mason](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason "Sandra Mason") was jointly nominated by the Prime Minister and the Leader of the Opposition as candidate to be the first [president of Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Barbados "President of Barbados"),[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-76) and was subsequently [elected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Barbadian_presidential_election "2021 Barbadian presidential election") on 20 October.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-77) Mason took office on 30 November 2021.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-78)[Prince Charles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_Charles "Prince Charles"), the heir apparent to the Barbadian Crown at the time, attended the swearing-in ceremony in Bridgetown at the invitation of the Government of Barbados.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-79)

Queen Elizabeth sent a message of congratulations to President Mason and the people of Barbados, saying: "As you celebrate this momentous day, I send you and all Barbadians my warmest good wishes for your happiness, peace and prosperity in the future."[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-80)

A survey that was conducted between 23 October 2021 and 10 November 2021, by the [University of the West Indies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_the_West_Indies "University of the West Indies") showed 34% of respondents being in favour of transitioning to a republic, while 30% were indifferent. Notably, no overall majority was found in the survey; with 24% not indicating a preference and the remaining 12% being opposed to the removal of Queen Elizabeth.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-81)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-82)

On 20 June 2022, a Constitutional Review Commission was formed and sworn in by Jeffrey Gibson (who at the time was serving temporarily as Acting President of Barbados) to review the Constitution of Barbados.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-83)

The commission was given a 15-month timeline to complete its work, which included consulting the public about the new republic and drafting a constitution.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-84) Thus, the CRC engaged the public in a number of public meetings, lectures, and [Twitter Spaces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter_Spaces "Twitter Spaces").[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-85) The report was announced delayed by August 2023,[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-86) with the final report submitted 30 June 2024.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-87)

In February 2026, prime minister Mia Mottley won her third consecutive [election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Barbadian_general_election "2026 Barbadian general election") victory by landslide, meaning her Barbados Labour party won again all the 30 seats in the [House of Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Assembly_of_Barbados "House of Assembly of Barbados").[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-88)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Barbados&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Geography")]

Main article: [Geography of Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geography_of_Barbados "Geography of Barbados")

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Barbados-2022_englisch.png/330px-Barbados-2022_englisch.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Barbados-2022_englisch.png)

Map of Barbados

Barbados is situated in the Atlantic Ocean, east of the other [West Indies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Indies "West Indies") Islands. Barbados is the easternmost island in the [Lesser Antilles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lesser_Antilles "Lesser Antilles") in the southern Caribbean area. It is 21 miles (34 kilometres) long and up to 23 km (14 mi) wide, covering an area of 439 km 2 (169 sq mi).[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-89) It lies about 168 km (104 mi) east of both the countries of [Saint Lucia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Lucia "Saint Lucia") and [Saint Vincent and the Grenadines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Vincent_and_the_Grenadines "Saint Vincent and the Grenadines"); 180 km (110 mi) south-east of [Martinique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martinique "Martinique") and 400 km (250 mi) north-east of [Trinidad and Tobago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinidad_and_Tobago "Trinidad and Tobago"). It is flat in comparison to its island neighbours to the west, the [Windward Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windward_Islands "Windward Islands"). The island rises gently to the central highland region known as Scotland District, with the highest point being [Mount Hillaby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Hillaby "Mount Hillaby")340 m (1,120 ft) above sea level.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Encylopedia_Britannica-_Barbados-29)

In Barbados, [forest cover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest_cover "Forest cover") is around 15% of the total land area, equivalent to 6,300 hectares (ha) of forest in 2020, which was unchanged from 1990. In 2020, naturally regenerating forest covered 6,300 hectares (ha) and planted forest covered 0 hectares (ha). Of the naturally regenerating forest 0% was reported to be [primary forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primary_forest "Primary forest") (consisting of native tree species with no clearly visible indications of human activity) and around 5% of the forest area was found within protected areas. For the year 2015, 1% of the forest area was reported to be under [public ownership](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_ownership "State ownership"), 0% [private ownership](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_property "Private property") and 99% with ownership listed as other or unknown.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-90)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-91)

In the parish of [Saint Michael](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Michael,_Barbados "Saint Michael, Barbados") lies Barbados's capital and main city, [Bridgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridgetown "Bridgetown"), containing one third of the country's population.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Encylopedia_Britannica-_Barbados-29) Other major towns scattered across the island include [Holetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holetown "Holetown"), in the parish of [Saint James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_James,_Barbados "Saint James, Barbados"); [Oistins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oistins "Oistins"), in the parish of [Christ Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christ_Church,_Barbados "Christ Church, Barbados"); and [Speightstown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speightstown "Speightstown"), in the parish of [Saint Peter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Peter,_Barbados "Saint Peter, Barbados").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Barbados lies at latitude [13° N](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/13th_parallel_north "13th parallel north") and longitude [59° W](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/59th_meridian_west "59th meridian west"). The population tends to be concentrated around the southwest coast, with the interior more sparsely populated, due to the presence of the [agrarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agrarian_society "Agrarian society") focused socio-economic model during the colonial period attributed to sugar cane harvesting and plantation system dominant on the island.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-CIA_World_Factbook_%E2%80%93_Barbados-1)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_%E2%80%93_Barbados-92)

### Geology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Barbados&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Geology")]

Barbados lies on the boundary of the [South American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_American_Plate "South American Plate") and the [Caribbean Plates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Plate "Caribbean Plate").[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-93) The [subduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subduction "Subduction") of the South American Plate beneath the Caribbean Plate scrapes sediment from the South American Plate and deposits it above the subduction zone forming an [accretionary prism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accretionary_wedge "Accretionary wedge"). The rate of this depositing of material allows Barbados to rise at a rate of about 25 mm (1 in) per 1,000 years.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-94) This subduction means [geologically](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geology "Geology") the island is composed of [coral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coral "Coral") roughly 90 m (300 ft) thick, where reefs formed above the sediment. The land slopes in a series of "terraces" in the west and goes into an incline in the east. A large proportion of the island is circled by [coral reefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coral_reefs "Coral reefs").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-Encylopedia_Britannica-_Barbados-29)

The erosion of [limestone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limestone "Limestone") in the northeast of the island, in the Scotland District, has resulted in the formation of various [caves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cave "Cave") and [gullies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gully "Gully"). On the [Atlantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Ocean "Atlantic Ocean") east coast of the island [coastal landforms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coastal_landforms "Coastal landforms"), including [stacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stack_(geology) "Stack (geology)"), have been created due to the limestone composition of the area. Also notable in the island is the rocky cape known as [Pico Teneriffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pico_Teneriffe_(Barbados) "Pico Teneriffe (Barbados)")[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-95) or Pico de Tenerife, which is named after the fact that the island of [Tenerife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenerife "Tenerife") in Spain is the first land east of Barbados according to the belief of the locals.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Barbados&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Climate")]

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/Bathsheba%2C_Barbados_08.jpg/250px-Bathsheba%2C_Barbados_08.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bathsheba,_Barbados_08.jpg)

[Bathsheba, Saint Joseph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bathsheba,_Saint_Joseph,_Barbados "Bathsheba, Saint Joseph, Barbados")

The country generally experiences two seasons, one of which includes noticeably higher rainfall. Known as the "[wet season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wet_season "Wet season")", this period runs from June to December. By contrast, the "[dry season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dry_season "Dry season")" runs from December to May. Annual precipitation ranges between 1,000 and 2,300 mm (40 and 90 in). From December to May the average temperatures range from 21 to 31°C (70 to 88°F), while between June and November, they range from 23 to 31°C (73 to 88°F).[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-96)

On the [Köppen climate classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification") scale, much of Barbados is regarded as a [tropical monsoon climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_monsoon_climate "Tropical monsoon climate") (Am). However, breezes of 12 to 16 km/h (7 to 10 mph) abound throughout the year and give Barbados a [climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate "Climate") which is moderately tropical.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Infrequent natural hazards include earthquakes, [landslips](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landslip "Landslip"), and [hurricanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_hurricane "Atlantic hurricane"). Barbados lies outside the [Main Development Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_Development_Region "Main Development Region") for [tropical cyclone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone "Tropical cyclone") activity in the Atlantic, and is often spared the worst effects of the region's storms during the rainy season. On average, a major hurricane makes [landfall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landfall "Landfall") in Barbados about once every 26 years. The last significant hit from a hurricane to cause severe damage to Barbados was [Hurricane Janet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Janet "Hurricane Janet") in 1955; in 2010 the island was struck by [Hurricane Tomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Tomas "Hurricane Tomas"), but this caused only minor damage across the country as it was only at Tropical Storm strength at the time of impact.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-97)

### Environmental issues

Barbados was the twentieth most water stressed country in the world in 2022.

Barbados is susceptible to environmental pressures. As one of the world's most [densely populated isles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_island_countries_by_population_density "List of island countries by population density"), the government worked during the 1990s[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-98) to aggressively integrate the growing south coast of the island into the Bridgetown Sewage Treatment Plant to reduce contamination of offshore coral reefs.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-99)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-100) As of the first decade of the 21st century, a second treatment plant has been proposed along the island's west coast. Being so densely populated, Barbados has made great efforts to protect its underground [aquifers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquifer "Aquifer").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-barbadosadvocate.com-101)

As a coral-limestone island, Barbados is highly permeable to seepage of surface water into the earth. The government has placed great emphasis on protecting the catchment areas that lead directly into the huge network of underground aquifers and streams.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-barbadosadvocate.com-101) On occasion illegal squatters have breached these areas, and the government has removed squatters to preserve the cleanliness of the underground springs which provide the island's drinking water.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-102)

The government has placed a huge emphasis on keeping Barbados clean with the aim of protecting the environment and preserving offshore coral reefs which surround the island.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-103) Many initiatives to mitigate human pressures on the coastal regions of Barbados and seas come from the Coastal Zone Management Unit (CZMU).[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-104)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-105) Barbados has nearly 56 miles (90 kilometres) of coral reefs just offshore and two protected marine parks have been established off the west coast.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-106) Overfishing is another threat which faces Barbados.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-107)

Although on the opposite side of the Atlantic, and some 3,000 miles (4,800 kilometres) west of Africa, Barbados is one of many places in the American continent that experience heightened levels of [mineral dust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mineral_dust "Mineral dust") from the [Sahara Desert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahara_Desert "Sahara Desert").[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-108) Some particularly intense dust episodes have been blamed partly for the impacts on the health of coral reefs[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-109) surrounding Barbados or [asthmatic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asthmatic "Asthmatic") episodes,[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-110) but evidence has not wholly supported the former claim.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-111)

Access to [biocapacity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biocapacity "Biocapacity") in Barbados is much lower than world average. In 2016, Barbados had 0.17 global hectares[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-footprintdata-112) of biocapacity per person within its territory, much less than the world average of 1.6 global hectares per person.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-113) In 2016 Barbados used 0.84 global hectares of biocapacity per person - their [ecological footprint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecological_footprint "Ecological footprint") of consumption. This means they use approximately five times as much biocapacity as Barbados contains. As a result, Barbados is running a biocapacity deficit.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-footprintdata-112)

### Wildlife

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Barbados&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Wildlife")]

Main article: [Fauna of Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fauna_of_Barbados "Fauna of Barbados")

Barbados is host to four species of nesting turtles ([green turtles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_turtles "Green turtles"), [loggerheads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loggerhead_sea_turtle "Loggerhead sea turtle"), [hawksbill turtles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawksbill_turtle "Hawksbill turtle"), and [leatherbacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leatherbacks "Leatherbacks")) and has the second-largest hawksbill turtle-breeding population in the Caribbean.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-114) The driving of vehicles on beaches can crush nests buried in the sand and such activity is discouraged in nesting areas.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-115)

Barbados is also the host to the [green monkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_monkey "Green monkey").[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-116) The green monkey is found in West Africa from Senegal to the Volta River. It has been introduced to the Cape Verde islands off north-western Africa, and the West Indian islands of Saint Kitts, Nevis, Saint Martin, and Barbados. It was introduced to the West Indies in the late 17th century when slave trade ships travelled to the Caribbean from West Africa. The green monkey is considered a very curious and mischievous/troublesome animal by locals.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-117)[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-118)

Barbados has been an independent country since 30 November 1966.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-119) It functions as a [parliamentary republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliamentary_republic "Parliamentary republic") modelled on the British [Westminster system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westminster_system "Westminster system"). The [head of state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_state "Head of state") is the [President of Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Barbados "President of Barbados") – presently [Jeffrey Bostic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeffrey_Bostic "Jeffrey Bostic") – elected by the [Parliament of Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_of_Barbados "Parliament of Barbados") for a term of four years, and advised on matters of the Barbadian state by the [Prime Minister of Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Barbados "Prime Minister of Barbados"), who is [head of government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_government "Head of government"). There are 30 representatives within the [House of Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados_House_of_Assembly "Barbados House of Assembly"), the lower chamber of Parliament. In the [Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_of_Barbados "Senate of Barbados"), the upper chamber of Parliament, there are 21 senators.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-120)

The [Constitution of Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Barbados "Constitution of Barbados") is the supreme law of the country.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-121) Legislation is passed by the Parliament of Barbados but does not have the force of law unless the President grants their assent to that law. The right to withhold assent is absolute and cannot be overridden by Parliament.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-122) The Attorney General is the principal legal adviser to the government (according to s.72(1) of the Constitution.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-constitution-123) The [independent judiciary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judiciary_of_Barbados "Judiciary of Barbados"), known as the Judicature, is established by s79C of the Constitution.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados#cite_note-constitution-123)

During the 1990s, at the suggestion of [Trinidad and Tobago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinidad_and_Tobago "Trinidad and Tobago")'s [Patrick Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Manning "Patrick Manning"), Barbados attempted a [political union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_union "Political union") with Trinidad and Tobago and [Guyana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guyana "Guyana").
